title: Go-Bag
items: Water: 1 gal (4 L) per person per day, 3 days
Water filter or purification tablets
Food: 3 days of ready-to-eat, non-perishable food per person
Manual can opener and a spoon
Flashlight or headlamp with extra batteries
Battery or hand-crank radio with NOAA weather band
Phone charger cable and a charged power bank
First aid kit (see First Aid Kit list)
Prescription medicines for 7 days, plus a written list of medicines and doses
Glasses or contacts and supplies
Copies of ID, insurance cards, and important papers in a waterproof bag
Cash in small bills
Whistle
N95 masks
Change of clothes, sturdy shoes, rain gear, and a warm layer
Emergency blanket or sleeping bag
Hygiene items: soap, hand sanitizer, toothbrush, menstrual supplies, toilet paper
Multi-tool or knife and duct tape
Lighter or waterproof matches
Paper map of your area with evacuation routes marked
Printed emergency contact list and family comms plan card
Baby supplies if needed: ready-to-feed formula, diapers, wipes
Pet supplies if needed: food, water, leash, carrier, records
Spare house and car keys

title: Home Water and Food Supply
items: Water: 1 gal (4 L) per person per day for at least 2 weeks
Extra water for pets, hot weather, and sick people
Unscented bleach (6% or 8.25%) and a medicine dropper for treating water
Label stored water with the date; replace self-filled water every 6 months
Food: 2 weeks of non-perishable food you already eat
Canned meat, fish, beans, and vegetables
Peanut butter, nuts, dried fruit, crackers, cereal, and granola bars
Shelf-stable milk and juice
Ready-to-feed infant formula and baby food if needed
Food for special diets and allergies
Manual can opener
Camp stove or grill with fuel, for outdoor use only
Appliance thermometers in the fridge and freezer
Coolers and frozen water jugs or ice packs
Rotate food: use the oldest first, and restock
Pet food and water for 2 weeks

title: First Aid Kit
items: Tourniquet (commercial, such as a CAT or SOF-T)
Hemostatic or plain gauze for wound packing
Pressure bandage (trauma dressing)
Gloves, several pairs (non-latex)
CPR face shield or mask
Adhesive bandages in several sizes
Gauze pads and rolled gauze
Medical tape
Elastic bandage for sprains
Triangle bandage for a sling
SAM splint or other padded splint
Trauma shears and tweezers
Antibiotic ointment and petroleum jelly
Antiseptic wipes
Instant cold packs
Emergency blanket
Aspirin (for suspected heart attack in adults)
Pain and fever reducers (acetaminophen, ibuprofen)
Antihistamine for allergic reactions
Epinephrine auto-injector if prescribed
Oral rehydration salt packets
Glucose tablets or gel
Hydrocortisone cream
Thermometer
Eye wash or saline
Personal prescription medicines
Small flashlight
First aid guide (this app) and a printed copy of key steps

title: Sanitation Kit
items: Two 5-gallon (20 L) buckets with tight lids
Toilet seat that fits a bucket
Heavy-duty trash bags (contractor bags)
Absorbent: kitty litter, sawdust, or peat
Toilet paper
Unscented bleach for disinfecting
Hand soap and hand sanitizer (at least 60% alcohol)
Water jug with spigot for handwashing
Disposable gloves
Wet wipes
Menstrual supplies
Diapers and wipes if needed
Garbage cans with tight lids for storing sealed waste bags
Zip ties or twist ties
Small shovel for cat holes or latrines
Labels or tape and a marker

title: Car Kit
items: Water and non-perishable snacks
Blankets or sleeping bags and warm clothing
Hat, gloves, and boots for winter
Flashlight with extra batteries
Phone charger for the car
First aid kit with a tourniquet
Jumper cables or a portable jump starter
Tire inflator or sealant, and know where your spare and jack are
Road flares or reflective triangles
Ice scraper and small shovel
Sand, cat litter, or traction mats
Bright cloth to tie to the antenna
Paper road map
Whistle
Multi-tool and duct tape
Window breaker and seat belt cutter within reach of the driver
Keep the gas tank at least half full

title: Comms and Radio Kit
items: NOAA weather radio (battery, hand-crank, or solar)
AM/FM radio for local news
Two-way radios (FRS/GMRS) for each family member
Ham radio if licensed, programmed with local repeaters and simplex channels
Spare batteries or battery packs for every radio
Charging cables and a solar charger
Printed channel plan card for each person
Printed list of phone numbers, including an out-of-area contact
Pen and notepad for logging messages
Whistle and signal mirror
Meshtastic node, charged and paired, if you use one
Offline maps saved on your phone
GMRS or ham license printed or saved, with call signs

title: Evacuation Steps
items: Follow official instructions and leave right away when told
Grab your go-bag, medicines, phone, and charger
Bring pets, with leash or carrier, food, and records
Wear sturdy shoes, long pants, and long sleeves
If told to: turn off gas, water, and electricity
Unplug appliances
Close and lock windows and doors
Leave a note saying when you left and where you are going
Text your out-of-area contact before you leave
Follow official evacuation routes; don't take shortcuts
Never drive through flood water or around barricades
Check on neighbors who may need help, if safe
Text family and your contact when you arrive

title: After the Disaster
items: Check yourself and others for injuries; give first aid
Text, don't call, to tell family you are safe
Listen to local news or NOAA radio for instructions
Return home only when officials say it is safe
Stay away from downed power lines and report them
If you smell gas, leave and call the gas company from outside
Run generators outdoors only, at least 20 ft (6 m) from the house
Use battery-powered carbon monoxide alarms
Drink only bottled, boiled, or treated water until officials say tap water is safe
Throw out food that touched flood water or warmed above 40 °F (4 °C) for 2+ hours
Wear gloves, sturdy boots, and an N95 mask during cleanup
Take photos of damage before you clean, for insurance
Dry out wet areas within 24 to 48 hours to prevent mold
Wash hands often and keep wounds clean and covered
Get a tetanus shot if you have a wound and are not up to date
Watch for stress in yourself and others; talk about it and get support
Restock your kits
